explanation: Compute subtree heights in postorder. Return a sentinel of −1 immediately when a child is unbalanced or the child heights differ by more than one. A nonnegative height at the root means every node is balanced.
spaceComplexity: O(h) recursion space for height h.
attribution: Original C# implementation and explanation authored for EPI Practice from the displayed problem contract.
correctness: The recursive result is a true height when the subtree is balanced and a sentinel otherwise. If either child is unbalanced, the current subtree cannot be balanced. Otherwise the local height difference test plus the children’s inductive guarantees proves balance at every node.
walkthrough: For [4,2,7,1,null,null,9], the leaves 1 and 9 have height 1. Nodes 2 and 7 each have height 2 with difference 1 at their children. The root sees heights 2 and 2, so return true.
edgeCases: A subtree imbalance must be detected even if the root’s own child heights are similar.
A long one-sided chain is unbalanced once a height difference exceeds one.
